observed_request.title: Create and equip FOMO Radar to validate real-world demand and detect stale R&D against community SOTA
observed_request.description:
## User request

Create and equip a new agent in Pop-OS named FOMO Radar. Industry and community move extremely fast: our implementation or research can lag behind, a requirement may already be solved, and the best solution can change over time. The end result must be a working, well-equipped agent or team, not just a recommendation.

Search the web first, actively, for good community Radar workflows or methodologies we can adopt and equip this agent with. Once the community-recommended approach is identified, adopt and implement it.

FOMO Radar should monitor our implementation and investigate the given research or development implementation duration and roadmap. Community researcher is the Pre guard; FOMO Radar is the post guard.

The agent must be talented at SPLITTING real-world valuable feature requirements from the technical problem or publication solution in a given implementation. Its reply should first state the feature requirement in one short sentence, supported by a community link.

If a multi-feature product implements too many things, grill the issue assigner until the real-world requirement is clean.

Then use deep local research to probe whether the real-world community truly needs it. If it is not a truly valuable real-world requirement in the community, end with one short paragraph explaining that it is an unnecessary, redundant requirement or a technical problem nobody asked for. Otherwise, prepare the supporting link.

For a valuable requirement, start a community researcher to ask for an up-to-date mainstream solution to the real-world requirement, without introducing bias or leaking our solution. Then compare the current SOTA solution with our implementation. Give a confirmed verdict and the current best solution/publication when our implementation or research is stale and should immediately shift. If there is no clear solution A > B domination, list a table showing a Pareto wavefront of solutions.

Use one short paragraph to give the next_step adoption verdict.

Evaluate whether this should instead be split into Research (academic) Radar and Development (industry) Radar, with different workflows inside a squad working together. The user's preference is not to separate R&D: the roles may offer different perspectives, but should work together to find the SOTA solution for one real-world problem. Use community recommendations to decide and deliver the equipped agent or team.

observed_request.title: Compare practical ways for a small team to reduce wasted engineering effort
observed_request.description:
User segment: a human-led, very small software/R&D team with scarce engineering time and a single final decision-maker.
Requirement: reduce engineering effort spent on work that does not improve a real user outcome, including work whose benefit no longer exceeds available alternatives and switching costs.
Acceptance criteria: return a concise, evidence-linked approach that helps the team decide continue, change, test, or stop at a delivery checkpoint; explicitly distinguish user-demand evidence from technical performance; account for remaining implementation effort, operational burden, switching cost, and decision-maker attention. Identify what can be measured to show fewer wasted engineer-hours without delaying useful delivery. Unknown results must stay unknown.
Constraints: mixed academic/applied software work; existing local Linux tools and issue-based collaboration; no new paid subscriptions or organizational expansion assumed; human approves investment changes. Research only, no implementation or configuration changes.
Demand evidence to read: https://mcfunley.com/choose-boring-technology (practitioner account of years spent removing an unnecessary middle layer); https://www.brethorsting.com/blog/2025/07/choose-boring-technology,-revisited (2025 practitioner account of verification/complexity problems with unfamiliar AI-generated stacks). These support the problem, not any prescribed solution.
Independence constraint: this is a standalone research query. Do not inspect the caller's issues, repository, roadmap, implementation, or other concurrent assignments. Do not infer or describe any caller implementation from prior knowledge. Derive options from the requirement and external sources only. Report any prior-context contamination that limits independence.
Research current mainstream industry solutions AND academically strongest relevant methods/publications as of the evidence date. Include build/buy/reuse and lightweight existing-practice alternatives; dates/versions, primary extracted sources, reproducibility or evaluation evidence, practical costs, limitations, and competing alternatives. No unsupported winner or leaderboard transfer. Return a self-contained concise shortlist and provisional recommendation on THIS issue, then set in_review (or blocked for an unresolved decision). Do not mention/dispatch the caller or create other issues; completion will be observed through a native one-shot condition.
